forefront: Most Pentecostal congregations on earth are small, poor, locally led, and run by pastors who are not paid enough.
healthy: Pentecostal and charismatic Christianity is the world's fastest-growing religious movement.
history: Pentecostalism began in the first decade of the twentieth century as a movement of the powerless.
money: Giving is not framed as duty, gratitude, or solidarity.
reach: The movement's largest ministries own their own media — networks, publishing houses, streaming platforms, magazines.
techniques: Thirty named techniques from domestic-abuse and social-psychology research, applied to institutions, in the eight stages of the cycle.
loops: The seven loops below show how the practices connect, so that each step makes the next one easier and the last step feeds the first.
say-do: In the independent sector, no internal body has ever run it on a founder.
cost: The specific exit tax here is financial and irreversible.
ledger: They own the ministries, the property, the media, and increasingly the succession.
who-gets-hurt: They fall hardest on people with the least room to refuse and the fewest places to go outside the church.
tiers: Most of a ministry's work is done below the founder, by people who see how the money moves without deciding where it goes.
precedent: A register of prophecies with dates and outcomes would revise the rest.
questions: May I see the audited accounts for last year, including the founder's total compensation and any related-party transactions?
leaving: If you work for the church, get your employment terms in writing before you announce anything.
